newsitem.title: USA: Dole stranded behind Clinton as debate nears - Poll.
newsitem.headline: Dole stranded behind Clinton as debate nears - Poll.

text.p: Republican challenger Bob Dole was stranded 15 points behind President Bill Clinton and showed little momentum prior to the first presidential debate, the Reuters daily tracking poll said on Sunday.
The poll, conducted by John Zogby Group International, surveys about 900 likely voters over a three-day period to create a rolling average. Margin of error was plus or minus 3.3 percent.
"President Clinton is in a real comfort zone," Zogby said, because while his lead was down slightly "Dole doesn't seem to be moving at all."
"The real story of our presidential polling is that while Clinton's lead goes up and down, Dole is locked into the 30 percent-35 percent pocket."
Clinton is due to hold his first televised presidential debate against Dole later on Sunday.

When asked for whom they would vote if the election were held today, 47.3 percent said Clinton, 31.9 percent said Dole and 5.3 percent said independent Ross Perot. Thirteen percent were undecided. On Saturday, Clinton led Dole, 49.9-29.8

Clinton would lose support if he issued a presidential pardon to former colleagues over the Whitewater investigation, the poll said. Results over three days showed 33.9 percent would be less likely to vote for Clinton, 19.2 percent said they would be more likely to vote for him and 42.7 percent said it would make no difference.
Respondents gave a slight edge, a percentage point or less, to Democrats to control the Senate and the House. Zogby said the battle for control was "the real action so far this year."
"If Dole stumbles in the debate, he threatens to bring down the Republican majorities in both houses." If the election for president were held today, for whom would you vote, Clinton, Dole, or Perot?
